picks.editorial_note: An international team led by Mario Krenn showed in Nature that AI can design novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups — a striking demonstration of AI accelerating fundamental science discovery itself.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: EPFL's framework teaches LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty when proposing experiments, a meaningful step toward AI systems that can be trusted to guide real scientific decision-making rather than just generate plausible-sounding suggestions.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's autonomous research vehicle 'karl.' received a nationwide German testing permit — a regulatory milestone that signals growing government confidence in AI-driven autonomous systems on public roads.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Spin-off Black Semiconductor's graphene-based optical chips, honored with the Aachen Engineering Award, point toward a fundamentally more energy-efficient hardware substrate for the compute-hungry AI systems of the future.
picks.title: Light Instead of Electricity: Aachen Engineering Award for a Technological Breakthrough | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: A three-university NSF-funded effort (USF, Purdue, UT Dallas) to build quantum-resistant, AI-enabled security into next-generation wireless networks addresses a critical infrastructure vulnerability before quantum computing makes today's encryption obsolete.
picks.title: USF faculty secure $1.2M NSF grant to advance quantum-secure, AI-enabled wireless networks

picks.editorial_note: Helmholtz researchers' public call for Europe to build sovereign open frontier AI models reflects a growing policy debate over AI dependence on US and Chinese technology, with real implications for research funding priorities across the EU.
picks.title: Why we in Germany and Europe need to build our own open frontier models

picks.editorial_note: Federal cancellation of AHRQ healthcare research grants, including a Johns Hopkins AI project aimed at speeding lung-cancer diagnosis, illustrates how funding cuts can directly halt promising applied AI research with patient-safety stakes.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient

picks.editorial_note: Two Purdue AI projects were selected among the first awards under the federal Genesis Mission, signaling a major new national program directing government funding toward university AI research.
picks.title: Category: Research

picks.editorial_note: Princeton's finding that AI models misread key details in police bodycam footage roughly 1 in 4 times is a sobering, policy-relevant result as departments increasingly consider automated review tools for accountability and evidence review.
picks.title: AI tools can miss the mark on police bodycam footage

picks.editorial_note: UAB spin-out Spiromatics is commercializing AI-derived biomarkers for lung disease diagnosis, translating years of academic research into a real clinical product — a concrete example of AI research reaching patients.
picks.title: UAB startup brings decades of research to the future of lung care
